findings.evidence: No user video leaves the device. RecorderCameraX.kt:72-83 records a 2-second clip to the app-private file filesDir/temp/CameraX-recording.mp4 (file.deleteOnExit() at line 75). The file is passed only through RecorderState.Completed (line 100) to Controller.startRecording (Controller.kt:92) and CameraViewModel.startRecording (CameraViewModel.kt:95-99), where it is stored in UI state as recordedFile. Its only reader in CameraFragment.kt:67-68 is commented out, so openVideo (line 72) is never called. VideoFragment.kt:34-39 uses android.widget.VideoView and MediaController to play a local Uri and has no network path. A search of feature/camera found no OkHttp, Retrofit, HttpURLConnection, URL(, multipart or upload usage. In addition, the camera module is not linked into the shipped app: app/build.gradle.kts lines 119-158 do not depend on projects.feature.camera, which is referenced only by feature/camera/demo and micro-benchmark. The AudioExoPlayer.kt match is a false positive for this data type: it plays audio only, from app-supplied response and item sound URLs (ResponsesFragment.kt:113, ItemInfoFragment.kt:79), not user videos.
findings.recommendation: No Data Safety declaration is needed for videos. If the camera feature is ever linked into the release app, re-audit it, because it records video of the user's face and requests the CAMERA permission. Any upload of that recording would need a Data Safety declaration, and the Play form currently declares no data collected.

findings.evidence: The app does not read or transmit the user's music files. AudioExoPlayer.kt:100-110 only plays a URI given to it, and its callers pass game audio: hero responses (ResponsesFragment.kt:113, item.audioUrl) and item sounds (ItemInfoFragment.kt:79). Network traffic here is an inbound download of public game audio, not an upload of user data. ResponseRingtoneSetter.kt:57-79 writes such a response into the shared MediaStore after a user action, and its query at lines 48-55 looks up only the app's own file by name in the AD2 folder. DownloadResponseManager.kt:109-136 getResponses is the only query that could list other audio on the device, but it is private, has no caller in that file, and its result is discarded. No READ_MEDIA_AUDIO or READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE permission appears in the module manifests. The other two matches are false positives: Motion.kt:90 'track' is trackPress, a touch gesture modifier, and VideoFragment.kt uses android.widget.MediaController for local video playback in a module not linked into the app.
findings.recommendation: No Data Safety declaration is needed for music. Remove the unused private getResponses and reSaveResponseIn methods from DownloadResponseManager.kt so that a future audit does not have to rule out the MediaStore audio query again.
